objective: Measure whether replacing the shared global document-sentiment component with one fixed DistilBERT aspect-conditioned sentiment component changes the strict Count, TF-IDF, MiniLM, and E5 LOAO baselines.
classification: post-hoc protocol-matched component rescore using frozen prediction artifacts
research_question: For a fixed candidate-presence method, does aspect-conditioned sentiment improve held-out-aspect pair F1 over global document sentiment?

inputs.global_reference: The pred_pair_labels and selected_threshold fields already stored in the strict similarity-baseline artifacts.

protocol.prediction_representation: pair set; zero or one predicted pair per row
protocol.row_alignment: Require exact equality of split, row_uid sequence, held-out aspect, and gold pair labels between the two frozen artifact families before scoring.
protocol.sentiment_component: One shared frozen DistilBERT classifier over (review, held-out aspect), reused from the existing score-export run for every presence method.

fixed_threshold_component_swap.presence_rule: Keep each original validation-selected threshold and therefore every original present/absent decision fixed.
fixed_threshold_component_swap.comparison: Original global-sentiment pair predictions versus aspect-conditioned-sentiment pair predictions on the identical detected rows.

validation_reselected_system.purpose: Best protocol-matched end-to-end version after changing the sentiment component.
validation_reselected_system.test_rule: Freeze all 48 validation-selected thresholds before scoring test.

oracle_presence_sentiment.purpose: Separate sentiment quality from presence detection.
oracle_presence_sentiment.rows: Rows whose projected gold contains the held-out aspect.
metrics: accuracy on rows with one gold sentiment
compatible accuracy where the prediction may match any gold sentiment for the aspect

primary: fixed-threshold aspect-conditioned minus fixed-threshold global, per method
validation-reselected aspect-conditioned minus original global, per method
comparisons.reporting: Report mean percentage-point change across 12 folds and fold win/tie/loss counts. Do not claim statistical significance from 12 dependent aspect folds.

implementation_constraints: Do not retrain or alter any presence representation.
Do not use the DistilBERT selector scores or selector predictions.
Use only the predicted_sentiment field from the DistilBERT sentiment_features for the current held-out aspect.
Fail closed on duplicate or mismatched row_uids, gold labels, aspects, missing files, or non-finite presence scores.
Do not read test artifacts during validation threshold selection.
Write validation selection completely before test scoring.
stopping_rule: Run the four registered methods once. No method-specific tuning, alternative sentiment heads, or test-guided threshold changes.

result.primary_conclusion: With every original presence decision fixed, the stronger DistilBERT aspect-conditioned sentiment component improves mean test pair micro-F1 for all four registered baselines. The older negative result was specific to the shallow TF-IDF sentiment classifier, not to aspect conditioning itself.
result.secondary_conclusion: Validation reselection improves strict TF-IDF, MiniLM, and E5 further, but reduces Count mean test F1 because the Staff support: Email threshold moves from 0.02 to 0.07 and fails to transfer.

dissertation_adoption.decision: Aji requires aspect-conditioned sentiment for every active baseline.
dissertation_adoption.active_system_rule: Use the validation-reselected aspect-conditioned result for each method.

known_limitations: This is a post-hoc rescore designed after the original test results were known, so it is confirmatory only within the locked transformation and must not be described as a pristine preregistered test.
The reused DistilBERT sentiment model is target-calibrated through validation-model selection; the result is not strict zero-target-label LOAO.
All methods share the same aspect-conditioned sentiment artifact, so the comparison isolates presence methods but is not an independent end-to-end training run.
A singleton held-out candidate is evaluated per fold; the 12 folds together cover all canonical aspects, but this run is not a joint 12-aspect inference call.
